data.exact_reserve_text: The improvement is driven by benign catastrophe experience, beneficial developments of GBP 9.0m in prior year reserves and favourable loss ratios across the newly re-positioned portfolio. In addition, the resolution of certain legacy issues has had an appreciable favourable impact on incurred claims. Included within net claims incurred of GBP 68.5m (2014: GBP 83.1m) is an improvement of GBP 9.0m (2014: improvement of GBP 6.4m) to claims reserves established at the prior year end principally due to beneficial developments in prior year reserves across the Marine and Transport classes.
data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 1861 reported a gross prior year reserve release of GBP 9.0 million in 2015, representing a 4.0% reduction of its opening gross claims outstanding. This favorable development was primarily driven by a benign catastrophe season, lower than expected attritional and large loss activity, and beneficial developments in prior year reserves, particularly across the Marine and Transport classes. The syndicate also benefited from favorable loss ratios due to a re-positioned portfolio and the resolution of certain legacy issues, with specific favorable development noted for the 2013 and 2014 underwriting years.

favourable development of the 2013 & 2014 underwriting years
beneficial developments of GBP 9.0m in prior year reserves

beneficial developments in prior year reserves across the Marine and Transport classes

data.data_quality_notes: The claims development triangle calculation for prior year development yielded a different amount (-GBP 4.908m) than the explicitly stated narrative figure (-GBP 9.0m). The narrative figure was used as it is more direct and specific to 'prior year reserves'.
